item.title: Dragon’s Dogma 2 x Delicious in Dungeon Collab Adds Laios and Marcille as Pawns
item.description:
Dragon’s Dogma 2 teams up with Delicious in Dungeon, letting players recruit two members of the anime’s adventuring party. Find out how to get Laios and Marcille, claim their outfits, and when the crossover ends.

Delicious in Dungeon Comes to Dragon’s Dogma 2


Laios and Marcille Can Join Your Party


Dragon’s Dogma 2 has collaborated with Delicious in Dungeon (Dungeon Meshi), bringing Laios and Marcille into the action RPG as recruitable Official Pawns. As announced by developer Capcom on their website and social media on November 4, it arrived alongside Title Update 4.2 on the same day for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Steam, with the Nintendo Switch 2 version following on November 12.
Players can recruit recreations of Laios and Marcille from Riftstones located in towns and other settlements. Once hired, they function as support Pawns and can accompany the Arisen and their Main Pawn during their adventures. The crossover trailer casts Laios as a Fighter, placing him on the front line with a sword and shield, while Marcille appears as a Sorcerer who uses offensive magick spells.
Capcom has also added outfit sets inspired by the two characters, and players who logged in during the collaboration period will automatically receive these outfits in their player storage. Both the Arisen and their Pawns can wear the collaboration outfits, and any outfits claimed during the event will remain available after the collaboration ends.
The crossover is available in both the base Dragon’s Dogma 2 and Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen. According to their announcement post on X (Twitter), the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Steam versions will offer the content from November 4, 2026, until the January 29, 2027 update. The Nintendo Switch 2 version will run from November 12 until the same update. Laios and Marcille can only be recruited during this period.

Dragon’s Dogma Has a Long History of Anime Crossovers


Official Pawns Were Previously Used for Creator Collaborations


Before bringing licensed characters into the game, Dragon’s Dogma 2 primarily used its Official Pawn system for collaborations with real-world personalities. Capcom created recruitable Pawns based on content creators like Maximilian Dood, Asmongold, and FightinCowboy, as well as athletes from different regions, such as football star Shinji Kagawa and Japanese national volleyball players Yuki Ishikawa and Ran Takahashi.
Dark Arisen expanded the lineup with more international creators and characters from Capcom’s Capcom Collectibles videos, including funny depictions of Toy Leon from Resident Evil, Knockoff Ryu from Street Fighter, and the nightmare-inducing Real Rudy from Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection, showcasing the felyne Palico companion as an uncanny human.
The wider series has previously crossed over with several anime and manga properties. The first Dragon’s Dogma partnered with Berserk: The Golden Age Arc, adding weapons and armor modeled after Guts and Griffith. Berserk later returned for another series collaboration with the Japan-exclusive Dragon’s Dogma Online in 2018.
Dragon’s Dogma Online, which shut down in 2019, also collaborated with Attack on Titan and Overlord. The Attack on Titan event offered Survey Corps equipment, while the Overlord crossover added armor based on Ainz and Albedo, themed furniture, and a limited in-game event.
Dragon’s Dogma 2 and Delicious in Dungeon are a natural fit, with both following fantasy adventuring parties through monster-filled worlds where a good meal can make all the difference. Delicious in Dungeon fans ready to embark on their own adventure can check out our Dragon’s Dogma 2 Dark Arisen review below.

Dragon's Dogma X Post

item.title: GTA 6 Pre-Load Requires Up to 212GB of Storage, Rockstar Confirms
item.description:
Rockstar has outlined its pre-launch plans for GTA 6. Read on to learn when you can start downloading the game and prepare your console before its November 19 release.

GTA 6 Pre-Load Needs a Whopping 212GB of Free Space


PS5 and Xbox Pre-Load Times Confirmed for November 10


Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) will require up to 212 GB of available storage for pre-loading, according to Rockstar Games, which has confirmed that downloads will begin on November 10.
PlayStation 5 players can start pre-loading at midnight local time. Xbox Series X|S players, meanwhile, can begin globally on November 9 at 4:00 P.M. PT / 7:00 P.M. ET.
Players looking to purchase a physical edition can also expect code-in-box versions to arrive at retailers starting November 12. GTA 6 is scheduled to launch on November 19 for both consoles.
For more on the game's release date and time, check out our article below!

item.title: NIKKE PC Launcher Files Were Reportedly Compromised for Over a Month to Spread Malware
item.description:
NIKKE’s PC players who opened the launcher on or after October 23 may have been exposed to malware. Find out what happened and how Level Infinite responded.

NIKKE PC Launcher Reportedly Used to Deliver Malware to Players


Attackers Modified Files on Level Infinite’s Official Network


The Goddess of Victory: NIKKE PC launcher is reportedly compromised and used to distribute remote-access malware. Independent security researcher MotherSphere published a report on GitHub on November 4, documenting the incident using launcher logs, cached files, live server responses, and evidence submitted by other players. The official X (Twitter) account of NIKKE also confirmed that the PC Launcher's script files were tampered with by a third party, but client fixes and an update were already implemented, and that further details will follow.
According to the GitHub report, four JavaScript files hosted on Level Infinite’s official content delivery network (CDN), a network of regional servers that delivers launcher files directly to players, were modified on September 27. When the NIKKE launcher loaded the altered files at startup, hidden code could contact an outside server and download a remote-access agent, a type of malware that lets an attacker control parts of an infected computer from another location.
Images taken from MotherSphere’s post on GitHub
Once installed, the malware could reportedly run commands, browse and download files, and take screenshots of every connected monitor. Its available commands also included access to saved browser passwords and data stored by browser-based cryptocurrency wallets. These functions show what the malware could do, although investigators have not confirmed what information it actually took from each affected computer.
The apparent access to Level Infinite’s CDN has also led players to question whether other Level Infinite games such as PUBG Mobile, Delta Force, Honor of Kings, Arena Breakout, Age of Empires Mobile, and Undawn could be at risk. However, the investigation has only documented malware being delivered through NIKKE’s PC launcher. Still, many players are avoiding those titles until the situation is resolved.

Evidence Suggests the Malware Was Active Before the Anniversary Update


Level Infinite Appears to Have Quietly Replaced the Compromised Files


The earliest reported instance of the malware actually running on a player’s computer dates to October 23, meaning it was active before NIKKE’s fourth-anniversary update launched on October 29.
The technical report indicates that Level Infinite had already begun replacing the affected files. Three of the four compromised files were replaced with clean copies during the early hours of November 4. The main copy of the fourth file had already been cleaned on October 28, but two regional CDN servers continued distributing an older compromised copy for several more hours.
This means that players in different locations could temporarily receive different versions of the same file. Replacing the files on Level Infinite’s servers would also stop only new infections. It would not remove malware that had already reached a player’s computer.
Current reports are limited to the PC launcher, with no evidence that the native Android or iOS versions were affected. For more on the game itself, check out our Goddess of Victory: NIKKE review below.
Source:
NIKKE PC launcher compromise (November 2026)

item.title: The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel Title and Logo Officially Revealed After 8 Years
item.description:
Bethesda Game Studios has finally given The Elder Scrolls 6 a name. Learn more about what was revealed here!

The Elder Scrolls 6 Official Name Revealed


“The Next Journey to Tamriel Will Be in The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel“


The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel is the official title of Bethesda Game Studios' long-awaited next entry in the RPG series. Bethesda revealed the name in a video celebrating the studio's 40th anniversary, where director Todd Howard described the occasion as the "perfect time" to announce the title.
The reveal has been a long time coming. Bethesda first announced the game at E3 2018, more than eight years ago. The studio has yet to share further details about the game, and the announcement did not include new gameplay footage, a release date, or confirmed platforms.

item.title: Petit Planet Is Coming to Switch 2 in 2027 Before Genshin Impact Ever Made It to Switch
item.description:
HoYoverse confirms Petit Planet is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027. The free-to-play cozy life sim launches on PC, iOS, and Android on December 4, with Switch 2 details to follow.

Petit Planet Switch 2 Port Confirmed for 2027


We Got Petit Planet on Switch 2 Before Genshin Impact on Switch


Petit Planet is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027, which would make it HoYoverse’s first release on a Nintendo platform. The announcement arrives years after the publisher’s biggest hit, Genshin Impact, was promised a Switch version that never materialized.
HoYoverse revealed the news during its Petit Planet Pre-Launch Special Program on November 1. The game’s official X account followed with a post that read, "Let’s meet in the Starsea!" and carries the hashtags #PetitPlanetSwitch2 and #PetitPlanet1204. The announcement refers only to Switch 2 and mentions no version of the original Nintendo Switch. HoYoverse has named the year and has not yet shared an exact date.
HoYoverse has announced a Nintendo release before. In January 2020, months before the game’s launch, miHoYo announced a Switch version of the open-world action RPG Genshin Impact and shared a trailer for it on the official Genshin Impact YouTube channel. The game later released on PC, PlayStation, and mobile, but the Switch version still hasn't appeared nearly seven years later. Fans have joked about the missing port ever since, and the gag remains one of the community’s best-known memes.
The trailer’s comment section reflects that. Years after it went up, viewers still return to leave jokes about the long wait, from yearly "anniversary" greetings to Titanic-style "it’s been 84 years" quips and puns on the trailer’s "Coming Soon" tagline. Many commenters pointed out that the Nintendo Switch 2 arrived before Genshin Impact reached the original Switch, while others have said they gave up on the port long ago.

Petit Planet Launches on PC, iOS, and Android on December 4, 2026


Players on other platforms will get the game first. According to HoYoverse on an official X post, the worldwide release takes place on December 4, 2026, for PC, iOS, and Android as a free-to-play game.
Earlier this year, HoYoverse held Petit Planet’s second closed beta test called Stardrift Test, which, although a data-wipe test, allowed participants to keep specific chat history from the Café Untamed private room. After the testing ended, the developers thanked players who joined and promised to address their feedback to better the game.
Ahead of the official launch, HoYoverse has scheduled a pre-launch live stream titled “Petit Planet: Moving Preparation Special” for December 3, the day before release, which gives players a final look at the game. Anyone who wants to see more before the stream can check out our review of the Stardrift test below.
Sources:
Petit Planet Switch 2 Announcement
Petit Planet Launch Announcement
Petit Planet Pre-Launch Special Program
Petit Planet Release Date Reveal Trailer

item.title: Ocarina of Time Remake Reimagines Hyrule With Help From Its Original Artist
item.description:
Ocarina of Time’s remake brings back an illustrator from the Nintendo 64 original to create a new map. Find out how Nintendo plans to preserve Hyrule's new look while preserving its sense of discovery.

An Original Ocarina of Time Illustrator Returns for the Remake’s New Map


Veteran Zelda Artist Yusuke Nakano May Have Returned


Ocarina of Time remake’s new map was drawn by the artist who created illustrations for the Nintendo 64 original. Director HokWai Ng, who first worked on the Zelda series in Tears of the Kingdom, confirmed this detail in the second part of Nintendo’s Ask the Developer interview posted on Nintendo's blog on November 2. However, the company didn’t name the returning artist.
The strongest candidate is Yusuke Nakano, a veteran Nintendo illustrator who joined the company in 1992 and led the founding game’s character illustration work. He later contributed to other Zelda titles like Majora’s Mask, the Oracle games, The Wind Waker, and Twilight Princess, handling main character design and illustration.
His later Zelda credits include Skyward Sword, A Link Between Worlds, Tri Force Heroes, Breath of the Wild’s Ganon battle artwork, and the 2019 Link’s Awakening remake. Recently, he was credited as a field artist on 2025’s Kirby and the Forgotten Land: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World, suggesting that he has remained active at Nintendo.

The Remake’s Map Preserves The Feeling of the Classic


While recent Zelda games use large, seamless environments, the remake still divides its world into separate maps, preserving each location's identity and how the areas connect. The team wanted to update Hyrule’s presentation without losing the pacing created by leaving one distinct region and entering another.
Ng used the route from Kokiri Forest, past the Great Deku Tree, and into Hyrule Field as an example. "We wanted each new area to bring the same air of excitement that players experienced in the original. We hoped that moving from one map to another would provide a natural point of transition, giving players a chance to reflect on their adventure so far while building anticipation for the next part of their adventure awaiting them in the next area," he said.
Recent previews suggest Nintendo has modernized movement within those boundaries; major regions remain separated, but players can enter shops and other interiors without loading screens. Our own observations noted familiar areas like Kokiri Forest had subtle changes like a new training area in the shop and a new monument in front of the Castle Town gates.

Bigger Landmarks, But Clearer Boundaries


Extra Warp Points Were Removed to Keep Players Exploring Hyrule


The team still needed to make Hyrule feel richer on modern hardware without suggesting that every visible location could be reached. Art director Aya Shida said this became especially challenging in Hyrule Field, saying, "We wanted to preserve how it felt to explore the original map while using today's visual capabilities to make the world denser and more detailed."
To solve this, the artists added more detail to explorable spaces and reduced visual information in inaccessible areas. Distant environments therefore read as background scenery, allowing the remake to create a denser world without misleading players about where they can travel. Nintendo also deliberately enlarged landmarks such as Hyrule Castle and the windmill so players could read them more easily from a distance.
The importance of reading and traveling through Hyrule also affected the remake’s proposed fast travel system. Producer Eiji Aonuma initially requested additional warp points, but playtesting showed that the shortcuts caused players to miss discoveries along the way. "We were missing out on the moments of discovery that came from stopping along the way and wondering, ‘Wait, what’s this?’" Aonuma explained. He ultimately asked the team to remove all the new warp points.
Despite that, Nintendo has still added changes to the remake, such as integrating it with a smartphone or adding a new area where players can rematch defeated bosses.
Nintendo is going to great lengths to preserve what made exploring Hyrule so memorable in the original game, adding modern features while showing restraint over what it changes. With Yusuke Nakano speculated to be the returning illustrator, the new map could represent his modern reinterpretation of the Hyrule he helped define nearly three decades ago.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is releasing soon on November 5, 2026, exclusively on the Nintendo Switch 2. There's also a special 40th Anniversary Switch 2 edition and Ocarina of Time Amiibo with bonus in-game cosmetics.
Sources:
Ask the Developer Vol. 24: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — Part 1
Ask the Developer Vol. 24: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — Part 2

item.title: Silver Palace Releases Worldwide December 14; Free 4-Star Character Available at 30M Pre-Registrations
item.description:
Silver Palace launches worldwide on December 14, 2026 on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. A free 4-star character is up for grabs if the pre-registration milestone campaign reaches 30 million.

Silver Palace Launches December 14 With a Free 4-Star Up for Grabs


Silver Palace Arrives Simultaneously on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android


Silver Palace has an official launch date, and a free 4-star character is waiting for players if the game’s pre-registration milestone campaign hits its top tier. The open-world detective action RPG will release worldwide on December 14, 2026, which gives fans a little over a month to get ready for the city’s mysteries.
The date was revealed through the game’s official social media account, which teased the launch with the line “This is the golden age for detectives.” Publisher Elementa followed up with a press release confirming that the game will release simultaneously across regions at 2026/12/14 (UTC+8). Silver Palace will be available on Android, iOS, PC, and PlayStation 5 at launch, so players can pick the platform that suits them best.
The game is built on Unreal Engine 5 and will support 12 languages at release. Pre-registration is open on every platform, and the campaign attached to it gives the community a clear reason to sign up before the countdown ends.

Pre-Registration Rewards Include a Free 4-Star Character at 30 Million


The Pre-Registration Milestone Event is already live and rewards players based on the combined follower count across the game’s official social media channels. According to the announcement, reaching the 30-million milestone unlocks a free 4-star character. The rewards also include 20 Simulation Shots, the game’s pull currency for its character recruitment system.
Elementa’s press release states that Silver Palace has already passed 15 million global pre-registrations. That puts the community at roughly the halfway point of the top milestone, with several weeks of growth still ahead before launch. Each tier unlocks as the community reaches the matching number, so every new follower and sign-up moves the rewards closer for everyone.
Pre-registering is free and can be done through the official Silver Palace website or through the game’s storefront pages. Following the official social accounts also contributes to the milestone count, which makes sharing the campaign one of the easiest ways to push the total higher.
Silver Palace is an open-world detective action RPG published by Elementa. The game launches worldwide on December 14, 2026 (UTC+8) on Android, iOS, PC, and PlayStation 5, with support for 12 languages. Pre-registration is open now through the official website and each platform’s storefront.
Sources:
Silver Palace Sets Global Launch Date for December 14, 2026 - Elementa Press Release
Silver Palace on X (@SilverPalace_EN), “Silver Palace 12/14 GLOBAL LAUNCH”

item.title: Death Stranding Isolations Anime Announced for 2027 Disney+ Release With a Story Set After the Games
item.description:
Kojima Productions has unveiled DEATH STRANDING ISOLATIONS, a hand-drawn Death Stranding anime that follows a girl who shuns human contact in an America reconnected by Sam.

Death Stranding Isolations Anime Arrives on Disney+ in 2027


Kojima Productions Reveals the Story and Setting in a Teaser Trailer


DEATH STRANDING ISOLATIONS takes the world of Death Stranding into anime form and will stream exclusively on Disney+ and other Disney services.
The series was announced on October 29 through a teaser trailer on Kojima Productions’ official YouTube channel. The video’s description says “that world expands into new frontiers,” referring to the shattered setting Hideo Kojima created in the original game.
In the same description, the synopsis opens with the line “My mom became a crater.” It refers to the Death Stranding, the chain of catastrophic explosions that occurred when the dead crossed into the world of the living. Many survivors were forced into absolute isolation afterward, and the series centers on one young girl among them. She grows to prefer her solitude and avoids every opportunity for real human connection.
The story takes place in North America immediately after Sam, the game’s protagonist, reconnects the continent through the Chiral Network. The renewed connections bring “new and unforeseen consequences,” and the series follows several people who chose a different path from Sam and his Bridges comrades. They include an old man who connects people through a method that “defies all reckoning,” a female soldier “ensnared in a cycle of war and destruction,” and a boy who “seethes with rage at the absurdity of his life.” Chance encounters then launch the girl into a world she does not recognize.

Takayuki Sano and E&H Production Lead the Anime


Takayuki Sano directs the series, with animation by E&H Production. The studio’s earlier work includes NINJA KAMUI, BULLET/BULLET and the Magic Knight Rayearth television series, and the trailer description calls the result world-class hand-drawn animation. The cast, episode count and exact premiere date have yet to be announced.
Sources:
Kojima Productions, “DEATH STRANDING ISOLATIONS | Teaser Trailer,” official YouTube channel, published October 29, 2026

item.title: This Week’s Gaming News Roundup: Oct 25th to Oct 31st
item.description:
← Previous Week
(Oct 18th - Oct 24th)		This Week
(Oct 25th - Oct 31st)

October comes to a close with plenty of movement in the industry. It brought a new December release date for HoYoverse’s Petit Planet and an animated continuation of the Death Stranding universe. The Duskbloods has been delayed to 2027, and the future of established games also came into focus through an approaching service shutdown and a change in publishing. Several featured stories turned to the friction between developers and their communities, particularly when plans for PvP and endgame progression run against what players want from a game. These developments have plenty of time to unfold, and the conversations surrounding them will carry well beyond October.
Whether it's sinking 300 hours into a single campaign or diving into a mammoth expansion, this week’s games prove that scale only works when backed by depth. Rich character arcs give new weight to classic journeys, and tight combat mechanics make deep investment feel worthwhile. Where things stumble, however, is in sluggish grinds and half-baked survival features that fall short of their ambition.
Regardless, here’s a quick look at some of the week’s biggest gaming headlines.
Gaming News At A Glance
Petit Planet Launches This December
Death Stranding Isolation Anime Teaser Trailer Revealed
The Duskbloods Release Delayed To Further Enhance Core Concepts
Phantom Blade Zero Protagonist Soul Is Now Voiced by Sonic
Palworld’s Pocketpair Open to Releasing the Game on Switch 2
Other News and Developments This Week
Review Roundup: Oct 25th to Oct 31st
Good at What They Do, Less Sure of What Comes Next
  • ANOMALITH
  • Phantom Blade Zero
  • Monster Hunter Outlanders

Other Reviews This Week

Gaming News At A Glance: Petit Planet Release Date Announced, Death Stranding Gets an Anime, The Duskbloods Delayed, Phantom Blade Zero Protag VA Recasted, Palworld Switch 2 Is a Possibility


Petit Planet Launches This December


Petit Planet will officially launch on December 4, 2026, for iOS, Android, Epic Games Store, and Windows PC, with pre-downloads opening on December 1. Pre-registration is now available through the official website, where sign-ups receive a Bestie Star-Light.
Additional rewards will unlock as global registrations reach new milestones, with the final reward being a Sproutling Outfit at 10 million registrations. HoYoverse will also host a Pre-Launch Special Program on November 1, with more rewards and surprises teased for the broadcast.

Death Stranding Isolation Anime Teaser Trailer Revealed


Kojima Productions announced Death Stranding Isolations, a new anime set to stream exclusively on Disney+ and other Disney services in 2027. Set in North America after Sam reconnects the continent through the Chiral Network, the series explores the consequences of restoring those connections through the lives of people who chose paths different from Sam and his Bridges comrades. Its story centers on a young girl who prefers isolation and avoids human contact. Her encounters with several other survivors eventually draw her into an unfamiliar world.
Takayuki Sano directs the anime, with E&H Production handling animation. The studio previously worked on NINJA KAMUI and BULLET/BULLET. Kojima Productions revealed the project through a teaser trailer on October 29, though the voice cast, episode count, and exact premiere date remain unannounced.

The Duskbloods Release Delayed To Further Enhance Core Concepts


FromSoftware has pushed The Duskbloods out of its planned 2026 release window, with the Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive now targeting 2027. Feedback from the August network test has given the studio more to address in its eight-player PvPvE matches, where players earn Victory Points through direct confrontations or by outmaneuvering their rivals. Some boss encounters also encourage temporary alliances between competing players. FromSoftware plans to use the extra development time to refine these non-combat strategies and the rules governing each match. A specific release date has yet to be announced.

Phantom Blade Zero Protagonist Soul Is Now Voiced by Sonic


Roger Craig Smith is now the English voice of Soul, the former elite assassin at the center of Phantom Blade Zero. Best known for voicing Sonic the Hedgehog since 2010, Smith has also played Ezio Auditore in Assassin's Creed and Batman in Arkham Origins. His casting replaces Jay Maksenuk, whose performance appeared in earlier trailers and preview footage. S-GAME has yet to explain the change ahead of the game's release.

Palworld’s Pocketpair Open to Releasing the Game on Switch 2


Palworld could eventually make its way to Nintendo Switch 2, as Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe has reiterated the studio's interest in the platform. In an October 27 interview with VGC, he praised the console as an "amazing platform" for Japan's game industry and said Pocketpair would love to discuss a potential release. No Switch 2 version has been officially announced.
Pocketpair previously considered Nintendo hardware as a potential home for the game, and the studio has also expressed interest in expanding to more handheld devices. A Switch 2 release remains possible, with further details depending on future discussions between the studio and Nintendo.

Other News and Developments This Week


  • Pokémon UNITE’s End of Service Coming in 2027, and Players Are Disappointed
  • Blue Archive JP’s Publisher Switch to Nexon in January 2027 Brings Mixed Reactions
  • Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen Could’ve Been So Much Better If It Was Strictly Post-Game Content
  • Aniimo is Pushing for PvP in its Next Update, But Players Don't Want It
  • Poppy Playtime Chapter 6: Are Escape From Playtime Players Building A Better Place?
  • Aniimo Is Getting PvP, But Can The Community Handle The Toxicity?
  • Aniimo's Endgame Direction is Alienating its Core Community, and the Oct 29 Update Might Make it Worse
  • Aion 2’s Healer Shortage Starts With How It Treats Clerics
  • Silver Palace Releases Worldwide December 14; Free 4-Star Character Available at 30M Pre-Registrations

Review Roundup: Oct 25th to Oct 31st


Good at What They Do, Less Sure of What Comes Next


A game's strongest idea can make a lasting impression, even when the rest of the experience struggles to keep pace. This week's reviews have some interesting examples, from a monster-hunting game that gets the thrill of the chase right to a survival-horror shooter whose gunplay deserves better systems around it. A new expansion gives an already enormous adventure room to grow, and a long-awaited story finally brings its central character's past into focus. But the difference lies in how well each game turns its best ideas into an experience worth remembering.

ANOMALITH


An apartment block with inverted gravity and a shopping street that repeats endlessly are among the spaces Reona Minazuki explores in ANOMALITH. The third-person survival shooter follows her work as a Diver for the government’s Anomaly Zone Countermeasures Office. She joined to find her missing friend Arisa, and each expedition takes her deeper into these warped spaces to fight their inhabitants and recover materials for weapon and gear upgrades.
The best part of ANOMALITH is easily its gunplay. Deciding which threats to take down first and picking off weak points makes every firefight feel sharp, and there’s plenty of room to mess around with different builds. Reona's arc and the shady agency behind her ground the story nicely, but the campaign wraps up so fast that major reveals barely have room to breathe. Plus, once you get overpowered, the actual scares stop landing entirely.

Phantom Blade Zero


In Phantom Blade Zero, Soul has 66 days to clear his name after being framed for his master's murder. His search for the truth takes him across the Wulin, a martial world where traditional kung fu shares the stage with industrial machinery and mechanical horrors. Its kungfupunk setting gives the journey an industrial edge that feels tailor-made for an extravagant martial arts film.
Phantom Blade Zero knows exactly how cool it wants Soul to look. Its cinematic boss fights can escalate from tightly choreographed duels to spectacle bordering on the absurd, and its wide weapon selection gives the combat plenty of personality. The forgiving difficulty and extensive accessibility options make it an inviting entry point for newcomers; genre veterans may find the action too lenient. The main story is easy to follow, though its expanding cast and dense terminology muddy some developments. For S-Game, whose earlier releases were largely mobile games, this is a remarkably polished debut with plenty of promise for what comes next.

Monster Hunter Outlanders


Radiantite gives Aesoland an unusual ecology, with the island's deposits linked to a new class of monsters known as Radiant Species. Monster Hunter Outlanders builds its mobile hunts around this setting, pairing familiar weapons with original Adventurers whose specialized skills change how each weapon plays. Players explore the island, hunt its monsters, and gather materials to develop their roster.
The combat gets the fundamentals right. Monster attacks are satisfying to read and respond to, and the Adventurers give players a good reason to try different approaches to a hunt. The monster designs also translate well to mobile. Aesoland's mystery keeps the main story moving, though the Bond episodes mostly recount individual backstories and leave the cast short on chemistry. Developing several Adventurers takes considerable time and resources, with materials, Zenny, and Energy making roster progression a persistent grind.

item.title: New Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Commercials Show Off Ganon With His Organ and Flashy Combat Footage
item.description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake received two official commercials ahead of its release. Find out more about the new footage it includes.

Ocarina of Time Remake Gets Two Commercials Ahead of Its November 5 Release


Ocarina of Time Remake Recreates Ganondorf’s Dramatic Boss Fight


The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has received two official commercials ahead of its release. Posted on Nintendo Japan’s X (Twitter) account on October 16 and detailed on their website, the first video, titled "Ocarina," revisits footage previously shown in trailers. However, the "Battle" commercial features mostly new footage, offering a closer look at Ganondorf and showcasing the visual overhaul for several returning enemies.
The 30-second Battle commercial opens with Ganondorf playing the pipe organ. Close-ups of his fingers moving across the keys lead into a wider shot of the towering instrument. The footage appears to recreate the original N64 game’s pre-battle cutscene at the top of Ganon’s Tower, where Link discovers Ganondorf playing the organ immediately before their fight. The villain appears again later in the commercial, raising his hand as the Triforce mark glows with purple energy.

New Footage Teases A Few Bosses Like Morpha and Dark Link


Nintendo shows new footage that wasn't present in our last trailer breakdown. The new boss footage includes Morpha, the Water Temple’s boss, showing its watery tentacle wrapping around Link and lifting him off the platform, with the creature’s red weak spot visible inside the translucent water. Dark Link also appears in the Water Temple’s mist-covered arena, dodging Link’s sword thrust with a front flip and landing on top of the weapon.
Bongo Bongo gets a brief combat showcase of its own, with the Shadow Temple boss’s enormous disembodied hands attacking across the drum arena as Link dodges. The montage also includes Poe hunting on horseback at night in Hyrule Field, where Link can bottle and sell their souls for a hefty amount of Rupees in the original game.
Beyond the enemy encounters, the commercial shows Sheik being carried away by a shadowy attack. In the next shot, Link protects Sheik, sword drawn, as nearby structures burn. Finally, the closing sequence shows Link and Navi looking toward the imposing, burning castle as dark clouds gather above it.
Official commercials for the remake join the recent press preview, giving excited fans more snippets of the upcoming remake. In just three weeks, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launches on November 5, 2026, exclusively for Nintendo Switch 2. Pre-orders for the Zelda 2 anniversary Switch 2 and accompanying Amiibo are up now.

Nintendo Japan Ocarina of Time

item.title: Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Adds a Monster Museum With Timed Boss Rematches
item.description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake adds the Hall of Fallen Heroes, a new area where players can rematch bosses in a timed challenge. Find out more about the new mode below and other information from the recent hands-on preview.

The Hall of Fallen Foes Gives Hyrule’s Bosses A Second Round


Timed Boss Challenges Encourage Efficiency


The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s monsters are getting their own exhibition hall, giving players a new space to examine and rematch against the game's enemies. As shown in Nintendo’s newest overview trailer, released on October 14, 2026, the Switch 2 remake features the Hall of Fallen Foes.
This hidden location displays statues of enemies Link defeated throughout his adventure. Players can examine these statues for descriptions and information on where the creatures appear, but the main draw is the chance to challenge the game's bosses again.
King Dodongo demonstrates the feature in the video, with his entry offering a rematch button, a record of the player’s completion time, and an in-game timer overlaid during the battle. The trailer also offers glimpses of returning bosses, including Gohma, Phantom Ganon, Volvagia, and Twinrova.
Ocarina of Time 3D already offered a similar Boss Challenge mode, unlocked after clearing the Forest Temple and accessed by interacting with Link’s bed in Kokiri Forest to relive previous boss battles. These rematches were timed, and defeating all eight available bosses unlocked a gauntlet that challenged players to fight in succession. Other games in the franchise also featured timed boss challenges: Skyward Sword’s Thunder Dragon Lightning Round tracked boss clear times. At the same time, Echoes of Wisdom’s Slumber Dojo offered time-limited boss gauntlets and extra rewards for faster clears.

Hands-on Previews Reveal New Twists on a Familiar Hyrule


Ocarina of Time’s remake won’t be a 1:1 recreation of the original, with familiar environments, puzzles, and combat getting updates alongside its extensive visual overhaul. In our previous breakdown, we saw subtle changes like a bigger starting wallet, a possible fifth empty bottle slot, and enemies appearing in areas where they were originally absent.
Recently, Nintendo invited media outlets to play selected sections of the remake ahead of its release. Outlets report the preview ran roughly two hours and covered Kokiri Forest, the Great Deku Tree, Hyrule Field, Castle Town, and Adult Link’s Forest Temple. Those sessions revealed further changes in the remake, such as the Kokiri Sword chest, previously tucked into a corner of the boulder maze, now sitting on an elevated central platform players must jump to reach, as reported by IGN. In a separate breakdown, the site says the Forest Temple room now features guardrails that prevent Link from jumping onto a block before it rises toward the ceiling.
Nintendo Life reported that players can now summon a Business Scrub merchant inside dungeons using a Business Scrub Seed, which remains if they buy nothing. The Forest Temple also features a new lift in its block-pushing room, while the Poe picture puzzle no longer has a time limit. Additionally, jump attacks now involve a manual leap followed by a mid-air sword strike, instead of the previous Z-targeting and dedicated button to do the attack.
According to VGC, Hyrule's residents now have expanded dialogue and new interactions. In Kokiri Forest, a villager draws pictures of rupees and teaches a song that explains their value, while Castle Town’s bearded man now helps Link locate Talon by sensing other bearded people. Townspeople also display short dialogue bubbles as Link walks past, letting players catch their remarks without stopping to initiate a conversation.
These changes should freshen up Ocarina of Time for returning players, while new content like the Hall of Fallen Foes offers something extra for veterans who already know the 1998 original Hyrule by heart. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake releases exclusively on Switch 2 on November 5, 2026. Fans can now pre-order two new exclusive Ocarina of Time remake amiibos: Young Link and Young Zelda.

item.title: Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Reveal: What We Liked and Didn't Like
item.description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake got its first gameplay showcase at Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct. Here's a breakdown of what we liked, disliked, and where the fandom is split ahead of its November 5 release.

Ocarina of Time Remake Shows Off at The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct


The Ocarina of Time Remake's gameplay demo kept coming back to one tension: how do you modernize a 1998 classic without losing what made it feel like Ocarina of Time in the first place? Series producer Eiji Aonuma set that tone directly, describing the remake as a faithful interpretation of Ocarina of Time built with modern technology, a line that ended up doubling as a thesis statement for the entire hour. Almost everything shown afterward, for better or worse, comes down to how that tension between faithfulness and modernization actually played out. This was just one part of a much bigger showcase; see everything else announced at the Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct.

What We Liked About the Reveal


The expanded Castle Town was one of the clearest wins in the whole presentation. In the original, Castle Town was a fixed-camera area built largely from flat, static backdrops standing in for buildings players could never actually approach.
During the Direct's live gameplay demo, series producer Eiji Aonuma walked Link through that same space with full camera control, revealing new alleyways, additional minigames, and background structures that are now fully modeled, walkable locations rather than painted scenery. The extra buildings and detail didn't come at the cost of the layout longtime players already know, which is a harder balance to strike than it looks.
On top of that, the day/night cycle now runs continuously no matter where Link is, even inside towns, whereas time used to freeze completely whenever players entered one in the original. That said, Nintendo did confirm one thing isn't going anywhere: Aonuma noted directly during the demo that loading screens between major areas, like the transition from Kokiri Forest into Hyrule Field, were intentionally kept in to preserve the feel of the 1998 original, rather than removed outright the way a fully modern open-world game might handle it.
Dashing and jumping were both new additions shown off directly in the gameplay demo. Aonuma joked on stage about players rolling across Hyrule Field in the original just to move faster, noting that the roll button now doubles as a sprint when held down. Jumping got an even bigger overhaul: instead of automatically leaping off ledges the way Young Link always did, players can now jump on command with a dedicated button press, demonstrated as Link cleared gaps and small obstacles around Kokiri Forest that used to require lining up an automatic ledge-jump just right.
Link can also now toggle the Iron Boots, heavy footwear used to sink underwater or resist strong winds in the original game, on and off directly through a new BOTW-style quick-swap menu shown during the demo, instead of pausing to dig through a separate equipment screen.
It's the kind of quality-of-life fix nobody was loudly demanding, but one that should make traversal and combat feel noticeably smoother over a full playthrough.
Aonuma demonstrated this feature live by humming Zelda's Lullaby directly into the Switch 2's built-in microphone and watching Link perform it in real time, then followed it up by playing Epona's Song on one of the physical ocarina peripherals Nintendo plans to sell alongside the game.
It's a clever use of the hardware, and it's not coming out of nowhere: the Switch 2's microphone has already powered voice-based minigames in Super Mario Party Jamboree TV, and Animal Crossing: New Horizons' Switch 2 Edition uses the same mic to let players call out to island neighbors through an in-game megaphone.
Ocarina of Time's version is arguably the most intuitive use of that hardware feature yet, and it's likely to produce some of the most shared clips once the game is out.
During a Hyrule Field combat encounter shown in the demo, hits landed with noticeably more impact than the original's simple sound effects allowed, and small environmental cues layered on top of that, like a drawbridge slamming shut in the rain as Link approached Castle Town at dusk, added an atmosphere the N64 hardware was never capable of.
Navi got a functional upgrade to match: rather than just nagging Link to pay attention, the fairy can now actively call out enemy weaknesses mid-fight; a genuinely new piece of combat support that didn't exist in the original beyond her famous, often-mocked interruptions that served as one of the industry’s earliest memes.
The overall audio and combat refresh goes a long way toward making Hyrule feel like a tactile, lived-in place rather than a collection of looping background tracks.

What We Didn't Like About the Reveal


The biggest sticking point for much of the online reaction has been the shift toward a more grounded, semi-realistic art style overall, with the character models being where that criticism has landed hardest.
Zelda fans, ourselves included, were quick to notice that several character faces, including Link's and some of the shopkeepers', have a strange, slightly gaunt look that a large chunk of comparable to AI upscaling filters. One widely shared post on X asked why the reveal looks like it was run through DLSS 5, while another described the moment as a realism jumpscare.
Kotaku's own coverage went as far as comparing the visuals to an Unreal Engine fan project. It's not a universal complaint, but it's loud, and once you've seen it pointed out in the gameplay footage, it's hard to unsee.
The new quick-swap system for items and equipment is a clear win, letting Link cycle through gear on the fly the same way Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom handle inventory. The problem is that the full inventory and equipment screen players still pull up separately, which keeps a plain, gridded layout of item icons that looks visually closer to the original's utilitarian menu than to the rest of the remake's more painterly, atmospheric art direction.
Where the overworld now looks like a detailed, hand-crafted world, opening the inventory drops players into what still resembles a functional but flat spreadsheet of icons—a jarring enough contrast that it stood out even in the brief glimpse the demo gave it.
On its own, this is a minor detail, but UI is something players end up staring at for dozens of hours, so it's worth Nintendo revisiting before launch.
The new voice cast is a mixed bag based on the reveal alone, and the divide seems to fall along which characters previously had a voice at all. Ganondorf's new performance has been well received, with outlets covering the reveal singling it out as fitting the character, though who's actually behind it remains unconfirmed and contested. Some early coverage speculated the voice belongs to Matthew Mercer, who previously voiced the character in Tears of the Kingdom, while a separate report circulating on X claims it's actually Nick Apostolides, known for voicing Leon Kennedy in the Resident Evil remakes. Nintendo hasn't credited any cast members yet, so both names remain rumors rather than confirmed casting. Zelda's voice direction has drawn similarly positive reactions for matching how longtime fans always imagined her sounding.
Navi and Saria fared less well by comparison. Navi already had a handful of short, voice-acted interjections in the original 1998 game, most famously her Hey! Listen!, performed by Japanese voice actress Kaori Mizuhashi, but the remake marks the first time she delivers full sentences and extended dialogue rather than just brief exclamations. Per Kotaku's coverage, that shift struck several fans and outlets as genuinely strange rather than a welcome addition, since the Hey! Listen! delivery has become such an ingrained, meme-worthy sound on its own.
Saria's new voice got a similarly lukewarm response, with at least one outlet's own writer admitting the performance felt slightly off compared to how the character has always sounded in their head. It's worth reserving final judgment on all of it until more of the game is shown.
Nintendo's official press release confirms that ZELDA NOTES, a companion feature in the Nintendo Switch App, will support Ocarina of Time with a daily quiz, a virtual ocarina, and a location-hint system called Gossip Quest. The quiz can reportedly also be replayed using rupees earned in-game for extra attempts.
The individual features sound harmless enough on their own, but Zelda has always been a series built around exploration and discovery, a philosophy that's carried through even into more recent, more guided entries like Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom.
Layering an optional in-game checklist and hint system on top of that, even one players don't have to use, risks nudging players toward following a to-do list instead of stumbling onto Hyrule's secrets on their own terms, which didn't sit well with everyone on the team.

The Fandom Is Just as Divided as We Are


The comment section on Nintendo's official YouTube upload is full of fans in tears over the reveal. Comments praising the expanded Castle Town, the reactive environmental fog, and the overall whimsical fairy tale art direction are racking up thousands of likes, with many viewers saying the game looks exactly how they remembered it as kids, even though the 1998 original never actually looked anything like this. One highly upvoted comment argued that pure photorealism would have been the wrong call for a game like this, and that a distinct, stylized approach to realism is what makes the new look work.
Reactions on X (formerly Twitter) tell a similar story of excitement, with posts calling the reveal absolutely beautiful and comparing the new Castle Town to the dense, detailed towns found in other modern RPGs.
Plenty of the chatter has also been purely about timing: with the remake landing just two weeks before Grand Theft Auto VI, jokes about this is my GTA 6 and having OoT Remake and GTA VI in a two-week span spread quickly, even though the two games share little beyond a release window.
But scroll further into the same YouTube thread or search around online, and the tone shifts. Alongside the praise, there's a steady stream of jokes about the character face models and comparisons to AI-generated content, with some fans openly saying the art style isn't working for them. Some players see the remake as a faithful, worthy reinterpretation of a classic; others think Nintendo overcorrected into uncanny-valley territory with its character models. Both camps are vocal, and right now, neither side shows signs of backing down.

Final Thoughts


Taken as a whole, the Ocarina of Time Remake reveal showed a genuinely ambitious overhaul with several smart, welcome additions, the ocarina microphone feature and the always-on day/night cycle chief among them. That's bundled with some surface-level presentation choices that a large part of the fandom is struggling to look past.
None of it seems likely to derail excitement for the November 5 release, especially with a textured foil physical edition and amiibo support (Young Link and Young Zelda, unlocking masks based on the original N64 models) rounding out the presentation for collectors, but there's clearly some polishing left for Nintendo to do if it wants to win over the skeptics as thoroughly as it's already won over the nostalgic crowd. For a fuller rundown of how the remake stacks up against the 1998 original, check out our breakdown of 6 things the remake changes from the original.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake will release on November 5, 2026, exclusively for Nintendo Switch 2.
Sources:
The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct (YouTube)
Zelda's Ocarina of Time Remake New Graphics and Modernized Controls Are Dividing Fans (TechRadar)
Ocarina Of Time Remake Looks Like An Unreal Engine Fan Game And The Internet Has Thoughts (Kotaku)
Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Changes One Of The Most Iconic Sounds In Gaming (Kotaku)

item.title: 6 Things The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Changes From the Original
item.description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5, 2026, bringing along new changes while remaining faithful to the original. Read on to find out all the revealed changes during Zelda’s 40th Anniversary Direct.

Ocarina of Time Remake Balances Modern Conveniences and Preserves the Original


Link Gains Dedicated Movement Buttons for Running and Jumping


The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct offered an extended look at the upcoming Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, showcasing early story locations, gameplay footage, and new quality-of-life additions. The first significant change is that Link can now jump and run freely with dedicated button commands.
The gameplay showcased Link manually jumping between platforms on top of a pond in Kokiri Forest, whereas in the original, the hero would automatically jump when nearing an edge. Additionally, players won’t need to evade and roll through Hyrule anymore for traversal, as Link can now sprint.
Link was also seen diving underwater to grab a Rupee, the game’s currency, although this is more of a refinement of the old diving system rather than new movement. Link’s oxygen bar depleted rapidly, which could mean players will still need to acquire the Silver and Golden Scales to extend his time underwater.
Whether these additions are simply for keeping up with modern control layouts or will be used for new platforming challenges remains to be seen.

Threads of Time Tracks the Story and the Next Objectives


Nintendo added a modern gaming convenience that helps players navigate the often-confusing world: a story tracker and quest journal called Threads of Time. This new in-game menu chronicles Link’s progression and summarizes the big events in the story. It also pinpoints the next objective, showing the player where to go and what to do.
Finishing main objectives gradually fills out the tapestry, creating a visual representation of the narrative. While this is a fairly standard feature of modern games, the original game relied heavily on Navi, Link’s fairy companion, to guide the player where to go. Other quality-of-life changes to make navigation easier were also spotted, such as a minimap in the bottom right corner of the screen.

Link Gains the Quick Select Menu from Breath of the Wild


Combat in the remake remains recognizable from its 1998 release, apart from its visual overhaul. Link still uses the same kit of sword, shield, ranged weapons like the slingshot, and the influential Z-targeting lock-on system. However, the video showcased the quick-switching system used in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom.
Link will no longer need to pause the action, open the inventory, and assign equipment to the three C-buttons before using it in-game, as the remake introduces a horizontal item menu to swap between items. Additionally, the remake brings back Gyro Aiming for ranged weapons used in precision shooting, letting players aim by physically moving the Switch 2.

Cutscenes Are Now Fully Voiced


Ocarina of Time’s narrative presentation has received one of the biggest overhauls. Cutscenes are now fully voiced, replacing the original game’s mostly text-based conversations and character grunts with spoken dialogue during major story moments.
Nintendo is not simply adding voices to the existing script, as the remake features expanded cutscenes and additional dialogue. Characters have more to say, and the video showed off more conversations with Saria and Navi. Additionally, Navi appears to have seamless dialogue during gameplay, with the fairy’s text bubbles popping up naturally instead of stopping the action.

Hyrule Has Been Expanded and Fully Explorable


Hyrule and its iconic locations have also been expanded. Locations that previously relied on fixed camera angles have been fully remodeled for free camera movement, and players can now look around using the right stick. The video showcased Hyrule Castle Town, where the original used carefully positioned fixed camera angles and pre-rendered-style scenery to create the illusion of a larger, busier settlement. The remake doesn’t fake it this time, adding fully modeled environments and expanding areas that used to be backdrops.
Hyrule itself should also feel more dynamic thanks to a major change to its persistent day-and-night cycle. In the original, time stopped progressing in several locations, including towns, and would resume once Link returned to areas such as Hyrule Field.
In the remake, Nintendo says time will keep passing no matter where Link is, including inside towns. Nintendo mentions that "certain events only happen during the day or night," much like the original, so players can make use of the titular Ocarina of Time to pass through the day.

The Remake Makes Use of Switch 2 and Smartphone Features


Nintendo is also taking advantage of modern hardware in ways that go beyond updated controls and graphics. The Switch 2’s built-in microphone can recognize melodies that Link has already learned, allowing players to hum a song or play it on a real instrument and have Link perform the corresponding tune on his ocarina. Nintendo is even releasing playable and electronic Ocarina accessories designed to work with the feature.
Ocarina of Time will also support ZELDA NOTES through the Nintendo Switch App on compatible smart devices. According to the press release, its game-specific tools include tracking daily accomplishments and statistics, such as how many enemies the player has defeated; Gossip Quests for locating places from visual hints, then using the earned points to purchase music scores for the Ocarina; and the ability to play the virtual ocarina from the smart device. Outside the game, the app also includes an Ocarina of Time quiz to test player knowledge, letting them spend in-game Rupees for extra tries.
Another modern tech inclusion is Amiibo integration, letting players earn the Young Link mask and Young Zelda mask from their respective collectibles.

Bringing Ocarina of Time to the Next Generation


These are six of the major changes to Ocarina of Time, and this doesn’t include minor tweaks like Link starting with a 200 Rupee wallet in Kokiri Forest. Nintendo has been careful to preserve the original, updating the experience while removing outdated barriers and design conventions.
For now, the extended look at Ocarina of Time’s remake shows that it’s interested in making the game feel natural to play in 2026, rather than resembling a modern Zelda title.

item.title: Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake Gameplay and Release Date Revealed During 40th Anniversary Direct
item.description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake officially revealed its November 5, 2026 release date and extended gameplay during The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Gets Official Launch Date and Extended Gameplay


Explore Hyrule with Navi on November 5, 2026


The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (OoT) remake confirmed its November 5, 2026 release date and revealed an extended look at gameplay on September 8, 2026, during the series’ 40th Anniversary Direct. The remake of the 1998 N64 classic was initially announced during the June 9, 2026, Nintendo Direct, with a cinematic trailer packed with OoT easter eggs and a 2026 release window. Digital and physical pre-orders are now open on the Nintendo online store, priced at $59.99 and $69.99, respectively.
Series Producer Eiji Aonuma headed the presentation, introducing the remake as a "faithful interpretation using modern technologies." The new gameplay footage featured Link traversing Kokiri Forest and various locations in Hyrule alongside his fairy companion Navi, including Hyrule Field and Hyrule Castle Town. It also showcased new features and gameplay improvements, such as a new 3D art style, a rotating camera, jumping at will, improved swimming mechanics, a tapestry that fills in with progression, and more.

Visuals Redone with Realism and Nostalgia in Mind


The remake’s art style was conceptualized with both realism and nostalgia in mind, according to Aonuma. Outfits and equipment were specifically intended to emphasize texture and realism while staying faithful to the original game’s beloved aesthetic.
The inventory screen has also been reimagined, featuring a more minimalistic wood-themed display compared to the original’s classic multi-colored rotating cube layout. Additionally, a fully rotating camera will replace the original’s static framing, which was a design limitation of the N64 controller’s singular control stick.

Jump At Will, Swim, Dive, Roll and Sprint


Guided by his fairy companion Navi, Link can explore various locations in Hyrule and the Kokiri Forest. The Direct showed Link walking around Kokiri Forest, entering the Great Deku Tree dungeon (one of many dungeons in Hyrule), running across Hyrule Field, and exploring Hyrule Castle Town.
The remake allows more freedom of movement than the original by giving players the option to jump at will and swim and dive for treasure in any body of water. In the original, players were limited to automatic jumps between ledges, and swimming mechanics were more restricted.
An ode to the time-honored tradition of rolling to move faster from the original game, Link will roll before sprinting in the remake. He can also climb vines, throw items at enemies, and fight foes using the original game’s classic target-locking system. The original layout of the target-lock has even been preserved for nostalgic effect, along with loading screens between locations.
While Aonuma confirmed that OoT offers a different experience from Breath of the Wild’s open-world exploration, the remake notably makes some changes to the original’s map system. For one, Hyrule Castle Town now has a map of its own. Maps also appear to be readily available for dungeons, whereas they had to be obtained from chests before. The presentation did not specifically touch on maps while explaining exploration.

Quest Tracker, Tapestry, Mini Games, and a Playable Ocarina


A quest tracker called Threads of Time will be accessible through the menu in the remake, serving as a guide and archive for players. A tapestry will also fill out to chronicle Link’s hero journey. By way of side quests, Hyrule Castle Town offers mini-games and gossip for players to stick their nose into, and areas that were previously only backdrops are now explorable. Aonuma encouraged players to talk to as many NPCs as possible, as "everyone has a different personality." The presentation did not show gameplay of any mini-games.
Notably, time flows differently in the remake. While in town, time will continue to pass, whereas it stopped in the original game. Because events in-game are locked to the time of day, Aonuma showcased the power of the Ocarina of Time to change time by playing Sun’s Song. The Ocarina of Time was also shown to have other capabilities, such as summoning a horse that adult Link can ride with Epona’s Song.
Players can directly play the Ocarina by humming music scores that Link has learned into the Switch 2’s mic. Tying in with Hori’s playable Electric Ocarina of Time, the game also recognizes notes from instruments. The Ocarina is now available for pre-orders through Hori’s official website.
Aonuma concluded the presentation by confirming voice acting for all cutscene NPCs, sharing that the title screen theme will immediately be available on Nintendo Music, and most importantly, announcing the game’s release date.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches exclusively for the Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5, 2026. To stay updated on the latest news about the game, check out our article below!
Sources:
The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct 9.8.2026
Hori Official Store

item.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Coming 2026
item.description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake was confirmed to arrive later this year during the Nintendo Direct on June 9. Read on for more details.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Has Been Confirmed


Trailer of a Tapestry Weaves Together Lore, Confirms 2026 Release Date


The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (OoT) remake was announced during the June 9th Nintendo Direct with a fully 3D cinematic trailer. After almost three decades, the 1998 classic is finally coming to a modern console in 2026. Nintendo will reveal specific details about the game’s launch for the Switch 2 at a later date.
The 90-second trailer did not feature any gameplay, but was packed with classic Zelda lore. It begins with a narrative exploration of events depicted on a woven tapestry before transitioning into a fully 3D model of a sleeping Young Link, with the Triforce symbol glowing on the back of his hand.
Fans took to social media to celebrate the unexpected news. However, Young Link’s design and the trailer’s graphics drew criticism from some who weren’t thrilled with its seeming departure from the original game’s classic cartoonish art style. Even so, critical fans promised to withhold judgment until more footage is released.

Trailer Introduces Plot, Features Foreshadowing and Easter Eggs


The trailer weaves together Zelda lore with 3D visuals, deep-voiced narration, and nostalgic music. It begins by chronicling events depicted on a tapestry, suggesting that the events in Ocarina of Time have already come to pass and are now etched into the history of Hyrule, the series’ primary setting.
The narration begins by stating that Hyrule was created by beings of supreme divinity, referring to the three goddesses, Din, Nayru, and Farore. From these three beings come the three pieces of the Triforce, powerful artifacts that represent power, wisdom, and courage.
The Triforce symbol is later seen in the trailer glowing on the back of Young Link’s hand, foreshadowing the events of OoT, where Link comes into possession of the Triforce of Courage.
The narrator also talks about the Deku Tree, an ancient tree that watches over an ageless forest-dwelling species called Kokiri, who each have a fairy companion. Before transitioning into the first look at a sleeping Young Link, the narrator introduces him as "a particular boy who did not have a fairy." In OoT, Young Link initially believed he was a Kokiri, before later discovering his Hylian origins.
Later in the trailer, just like in the beginning of OoT, Young Link is seen sleeping. He dozes on a bed of hay and woven grass inside a tree, while dressed in a woven green tunic with a black leather layer on top. The layer is decorated with a swirling symbol typically associated with the Kokiri, pointing once again to Link’s initially believed origins.
Variations of classic OoT musical themes are also played at different times during the trailer. Saria’s Song plays while Hyrule is being introduced, and the Kokiri Forest theme plays when the narrator talks about the Deku Tree and the Kokiri. Finally, a version of the Hyrule Field Main Theme plays when the Triforce symbol glows on the back of Link’s hand, signaling the start of his adventure.

Shocking, But Not Surprising


The announcement was unexpected, but a remake of OoT might not be surprising for those who follow Zelda news closely. Eiji Aonuma, the current series producer, who has been a primary driving force behind every Zelda title since directing OoT, has been vocal about wanting to improve older titles by reimagining them for newer consoles as part of the series’ shift to a more non-linear formula. This shift began with the massively successful The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild (BOTW).
A 3DS remake of OoT was released in 2011 for the Nintendo 3DS, following Aonuma’s statement to Revogamer in 2009 that he found the beloved title, which is considered by many to be the best game in the series, was "not as good" as modern series entries.
In 2023, Aonuma told IGN that he "doesn’t put too much stock in the chronology of the series," and that The Legend of Zelda stories work best when people "interpret on their own." This shift to non-linear storytelling for both new and remade Zelda titles has proved commercially successful, drawing in new fans and record sales.
BOTW is the best-selling series title at 34 million copies, with The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom following at 21 million copies.
OoT holds the third spot in sales rankings among Zelda series titles, with 14 million copies sold across the Nintendo 64 and 3DS. To stay up to date on the latest news about the game, check out our article below!
Sources:
Nintendo Direct
The Legend of Zelda Sales Statistics
Revogamers Interview
IGN Interview

Fans Relieved Launch Date’s Confirmed, But Still Have Reservations


Many fans are glad to finally have a concrete release date. Although some admitted that earlier posts without one had left them feeling unsure about its release period, thinking the date would be delayed instead. Other players requested Switch, Xbox, and PS5 versions, as the game is only confirmed on mobile and PC for now. A few players have also reported being unable to pre-register on Google Play, but this has yet to be addressed.
Meanwhile, players who tried the beta also advised newcomers not to expect an Animal Crossing replacement. They say the beta put caps on how much players could build, farm, trade, explore, and earn and are hoping the upcoming version shows some leniency in regard to these limits.

HoYoverse’s Relaxing Life Sim Set in Space


Petit Planet is an upcoming free-to-play cozy life sim in which players look after a small planet of their own. Daily activities include farming, fishing, cooking, and decorating, while sailing across the Starsea lets players find new areas, creatures, materials, and recipes. “Fuzzy Neighbors” share the planet with players, and there’s also a Galactic Bazaar that acts as a social space for trading and meeting other travelers across the skies.
In our review of the Petit Planet Stardrift Test closed beta, we noted that the game showed plenty of promise, with its cute art style, fully voiced cast, and an interesting set of Neighbors. However, the build did feel rough in some places, with disappearing seedlings, quests that just end abruptly, and tedious item pickups when harvesting in bulk. Hopefully, the issues encountered will be resolved in the final build. For more on our thoughts on the Stardrift Test, check out our review below!

item.title: The Duskbloods Delayed to 2027 Due to Gameplay and Balance Adjustments
item.description:
The Duskbloods has been delayed to 2027. Learn more about the announcement here.

The Duskbloods Launch Window Moved to 2027


To Further Enhance Core Concepts, FromSoftware Says


FromSoftware has officially delayed its upcoming PvPvE multiplayer action game, The Duskbloods, pushing its release window from 2026 to 2027. According to an announcement made on October 29, the Switch 2 exclusive has reached its "final adjustment stage." However, the studio stated that additional time is needed to refine the game's rules and balance before launch.
This decision stems directly from player feedback gathered during the game's August 2026 network test. In a post on X (formerly Twitter), FromSoftware acknowledged "active interest in the core concepts of the game," while an accompanying post on its official website elaborated that the extra development time will be used to elevate its non-combat strategies and varied gameplay approaches to a higher standard.
The Duskbloods' online matches put up to eight players against one another and computer-controlled enemies in a competitive PvPvE format built around flexible strategies. A Victory Points system determines the winner, with players able to earn points through direct combat or opportunistic tactics that avoid confrontation. Director Hidetaka Miyazaki discussed these mechanics in an April 2025 Creator's Voice interview with Nintendo. Some encounters call for temporary cooperation against powerful boss enemies, and special events can introduce additional objectives with bonus rewards that affect the outcome of a match.
Miyazaki's interview came shortly after The Duskbloods was first unveiled on April 2, 2025. At the time, FromSoftware planned a worldwide release in 2026. The studio has since moved that launch window to 2027, with a specific release date yet to be announced. In the meantime, check out our article below for the latest on the game's release.

The Duskbloods Delay Announcement on the Game's Official Website

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero Casts Sonic VA Roger Craig Smith as Protagonist Soul
item.description:
Phantom Blade Zero adds veteran voice actor Roger Craig Smith, who portrayed iconic gaming characters like Sonic, Chris Redfield, and Kyle Crane, to its English dub. Find out more details about Smith and his co-star Donnie Yen.

Sonic VA Roger Craig Smith Joins Phantom Blade Zero’s English Cast


Smith Replaces Original VA Jay Maksenuk Before Launch


Phantom Blade Zero has added veteran voice actor Roger Craig Smith to its final cast as Soul, the main protagonist and former elite assassin. Smith is best known for his longtime performance of Sonic the Hedgehog, first taking over the role in 2010 in Sonic Free Riders and Sonic Colors, and lending his voice to the character in most mainline games including 2024's Sonic x Shadow Generations. He also voiced the speedster in the animated series Sonic Boom and Disney's Wreck-it Ralph movies. Notably, he didn't reprise his role for the live-action films, as actor and comedian Ben Schwartz took over that portrayal.
Aside from Sonic, Smith has voiced several other major video game characters, including Ezio Auditore in Assassin’s Creed, Batman in Arkham Origins, Kyle Crane in Dying Light, and Mirage in Apex Legends. He began voicing Chris Redfield in 2009’s Resident Evil 5 and reprised the role in several games through Resident Evil 6. Capcom has yet to announce who will voice Chris in Code Veronica's remake, leaving it unclear whether Smith will return or the role will go to David Vaughn or Jeff Schine, who voiced Chris in Resident Evil 7 and Village, respectively.
Before Smith's last-minute casting was discovered, Jay Maksenuk had been the voice Soul, with his performance heard in earlier trailers and preview footage. Maksenuk, best known as V in Once Human and Gideon in Love and Deepspace, has now been replaced for the final release, though developer S-GAME has not explained why.

English and Chinese Voice Tracks Available On Launch


Donnie Yen Involved Personally as Creative Consultant


Smith joins Donnie Yen (star of the Ip Man series), who portrays Mó Yuan, the father of protagonist Soul and leader of the Bastion of Mó. Yen supplied his likeness, facial performance, and full-body motion capture for the character, and recorded his dialogue. The Hong Kong action star has also served as the game’s creative consultant since 2023, helping shape its kung fu punk wuxia style and action design.
Yen’s involvement extended beyond his own performance, showing that he's all-in on the project. According to RPG Gamer's coverage of S-GAMES' Q&A, he brought members of his stunt team into the motion-capture process and helped refine Mó Yuan’s portrayal as a father, which special care and attention for the flow, aesthetics, and philosophy of the combat.
Early reviews have praised the game’s performance capture and synchronized English and Chinese voice tracks, although reactions to individual English performances have varied. Players will be able to hear Smith alongside the rest of the English cast by selecting the English voice track in the game’s audio settings.
Phantom Blade Zero launches on October 29, 2026, for PS5 and PC. Physical discs will also be included in 2027. For more about the game, read our review of S-GAME’s self-described "kungfupunk" action RPG.
Source:
Phantom Blade Zero State of Play dives deep into combat and the Wulin world
